Part 2&3 事件 EVENTS

Describe an occasion when you were not allowed to use your mobile phone

描述一次你不被允许使用手机的场合

⚠️ AI 范例，仅供学习 — IELTS 口语全程独立完成，背诵照搬 AI 答案会被考官识别为背稿。

Part 2 话题卡片

Describe an occasion when you were not allowed to use your mobile phone

  • When it was (是什么时候)
  • Where it was (在哪里)
  • Why you were not allowed to use your mobile phone (为什么不允许使用手机)
  • And how you felt about it (并谈谈你当时的感受)

问题与答案

Cue CardDescribe an occasion when you were not allowed to use your mobile phone

I'd like to talk about a time when I was not allowed to use my mobile phone, and that was during my three years of high school. The school had a strict rule that banned phones on campus, so from Monday to Friday, I had to hand in my phone every morning and could only get it back on Friday evening. The rule applied everywhere in the school, in the classrooms, the dormitory and even the canteen. The reason behind it was that the school believed phones distracted students from their studies, and they wanted us to focus entirely on preparing for the university entrance exam. Teachers would check our desks and lockers from time to time, and anyone caught with a phone would have it confiscated for a whole month. To be honest, I hated the rule at first, because I felt extremely bored without my phone. In the evenings, after finishing my homework, I had nothing to do, and I remember staring at the ceiling in the dorm, counting down the days until the weekend. However, as time went on, I got used to it, and I started reading novels and playing basketball with my classmates instead. Looking back, although I wouldn't want to repeat it, I think the rule actually helped me concentrate, and it taught me that life without a phone can be quite enjoyable.

高中三年学校禁止带手机，周一到周五每天上交、周五晚才拿回；学校认为手机会分散学习注意力；起初很无聊，晚上没事做，后来习惯后改读小说、打篮球，反而更专注。

Q2How do young and old people use mobile phones differently?

I think the difference is quite clear. Young people use phones for almost everything, like social media, games, videos and chatting with friends, so their phones are basically an extension of their social life. Older people, on the other hand, tend to use phones for practical purposes, like making calls, checking the news or using payment apps. Having said that, the gap is narrowing as older people become more tech-savvy.

年轻人几乎用手机做所有事，社交、游戏、视频，手机是社交生活的延伸；老年人主要用于打电话、看新闻、支付等实用功能；不过随着老人更懂科技，差距在缩小。

Q3What positive and negative impact do mobile phones have on friendship?

Mobile phones have both sides, I think. On the positive side, they make it easy to stay in touch, especially with friends who live far away, and they help people organise meet-ups quickly. On the negative side, phones can weaken friendships, because people may spend time scrolling instead of talking face to face. So on balance, phones are a useful tool, but they work best when people remember to put them down and connect in person.

手机对友谊有利有弊；好处是方便联系远方朋友、快速约见面；坏处是大家只顾刷手机不面对面聊天，如聚餐各看各的屏幕；手机是好工具，但要记得放下它。

Q4Is it a waste of time to take pictures with mobile phones?

I wouldn't say it's a complete waste of time, because photos help us remember special moments. However, I do think people sometimes overdo it, spending so much time taking pictures that they forget to enjoy the moment itself. In my country, it's common to see people filming entire concerts through their phones instead of watching the show. So I'd say taking a few photos is fine, but it becomes a waste when it replaces real experience.

拍照不完全是浪费时间，照片帮我们记住特别时刻，多年后看假期照片能唤起回忆；但有人过度，只顾拍照忘了享受当下，如整场演唱会都举着手机拍；拍几张可以，取代真实体验才是浪费。

Q5Do you think it is necessary to have laws on the use of mobile phones?

Yes, I think some laws are necessary, especially for safety. For example, many countries have banned using phones while driving, because distracted driving causes serious accidents. Having said that, I don't think laws should control every aspect of phone use, because that would be too restrictive. So on the whole, laws should focus on situations where phone use clearly harms others, rather than on personal habits.

有些法律是必要的，尤其为安全，如多国禁止开车用手机，因为分心驾驶导致严重事故；医院、影院等场所也需限制；但法律不应管到所有细节，应聚焦明显危害他人的情形。

Q6What are examples of good and poor phone manners?

Good phone manners include keeping your phone on silent in meetings, not checking it while someone is talking to you, and stepping outside to take a call. Poor manners, on the other hand, include playing loud videos in public, answering calls during a conversation, or scrolling through your phone at the dinner table. I think these manners matter because they show respect for the people around you.

好的手机礼仪包括会议静音、别人说话时不看手机、接电话到外面；坏礼仪包括公共场合外放视频、谈话中接电话、饭桌上刷手机；我国认为家庭聚餐用手机不礼貌，礼仪体现对身边人的尊重。

Q7How does the internet benefit people?

The internet benefits people in countless ways, I think. It gives us instant access to information, so we can learn almost anything online, from cooking to coding. It also connects people across the world, which is especially valuable for families separated by distance. Having said that, the internet has downsides too, like misinformation and addiction, but on the whole, its benefits clearly outweigh the problems.

互联网好处无数；让我们即时获取信息，几乎什么都能在线学；连接世界各地的人，对异地家庭尤其宝贵；我国网购、支付、预订都很方便；虽有虚假信息和成瘾等弊端，但总体利大于弊。
